findings: Scope/hygiene verified: the task is test-only. No production source, csproj, props/targets, solution, package manifest, or packages.lock.json changed. git diff/untracked shows only the seven new tests/ArrTags.Tests/RendererBehavior*.cs files plus PLANS.md, README.md, docs/changelog.md, and the worker report. The pre-existing .opencode/agents/*.md edits (orchestrator model/effort, task-selection, recovery) remain unstaged and unrelated to 4.6. No RenderVersion/RenderOutputPolicy default or ADR-009/010 change.

Dimensions: genuinely covered. The unguarded theory GeometryScaleIsAppliedUniformlyWithoutAnOutputSizeBranch hardcodes independent expected scales (320->0.5, 500->0.5, 1000->1.0, 2000->2.0, 5000->4.0) and asserts the engine scale plus PillHeight/OuterInset scaling, so it would fail on a wrong clamp/reference. Five guarded renders assert oriented source dimensions, result Width/Height, and independently parsed IHDR dimensions for 320x480, 2000x3000, 720x480 alpha, EXIF orientation-3 (600x900), and EXIF orientation-8 (900x600, axis swap). This proves no upscale/downscale and oriented-dimension preservation.

Format: structural assertions are real and independent. The tests parse the PNG signature, IHDR length/type/bit-depth/color-type/compression/filter/interlace fields, walk chunk lengths to collect chunk types, and decode pixels with SKBitmap. Hardcoded expectations (bit depth 8, color type 2 opaque vs 6 meaningful-alpha, non-interlace, sRGB present, IEND last) are discriminating. Straight-alpha is verified by requiring alpha 128 and per-channel RGB within +/-1 of the source straight values, which fails on premultiplied output. The hand-crafted BuildHiddenRgbPng produces valid straight-alpha bytes with hidden non-zero RGB on a fully transparent pixel via direct zlib+CRC construction (bypassing Skia canonicalization), and the test asserts the rendered pixel is exactly (0,0,0,0).

Format limitation (non-blocking): the AssertNoRetainedSourceMetadata checks assert the output lacks iCCP/eXIf/tIME/tEXt/zTXt/iTXt chunks, but the synthetic sources themselves carry none of those chunks, so the suite does not independently prove stripping from a metadata-bearing source. This mirrors the existing task-4.9 OutputPngDeclaresSrgbAndStripsMetadataChunks test and is consistent with task 4.11 owning the golden/metadata/ICC oracle; it is not a 4.6 acceptance gap.

Truncation: genuinely covered with independent hand-computed expectations. A 40-scalar resolved custom badge normalizes to 21 scalars + '...' (24 total, WasTruncated true); a within-limit 24-scalar value is returned unchanged; '  WEB\u0000-DL\t\t1080p  ' normalizes to 'WEB-DL 1080p'; an unfittable widest-scalar value is omitted without expanding the surviving lower-priority value; width-fitting further shortens an over-wide 24-scalar label while staying <=24 and ending in '...'; and a 22-emoji label never splits a surrogate pair (well-formed UTF-16 asserted).

Layout: genuinely covered. Hardcoded row expectations pin three pills per row over two rows [0,0,0,1,1,1], lower-priority omission at six pills (v1..v6 from eight), monotonic row order, bottom-left anchoring (X==inset, Y==height-inset-pillHeight, row-gap spacing), top-right status placement (X+Width==width-inset, Y==inset, Row==-1), and non-overlap. A pure theory independently computes inset via BadgeGeometry.ComputeScale and asserts every pill's rectangle stays inside the safe area for 240x600, 320x480, 1000x150, 1000x1500, and 2000x3000. Minor non-blocking note: for the 1000x150 case the status pill reserves the only row so no technical pills are produced and the overlap loop is vacuous there; the separate safe-area theory still asserts technical pills are non-empty for that size without a status pill.

Cancellation: the tested contract is genuine and discriminating. The four cases prove a pre-cancelled token returns exactly Failed(Cancelled) with HasArtifact false, empty PngBytes, null ContentType/OutputHash/OutputFingerprint/PassThroughReason, zero Width/Height, and byte-identical source; and that cancellation wins over IneligibleSurface, SourceByteLimitExceeded, ContrastTooLow, and the NoMetadata/SourceUnavailable pass-through path. Declared limitation assessed as acceptable: because RenderAsync performs one synchronous bounded render before returning Task.FromResult, a token that fires after entry is not deterministically observable; the later after-decode/between-layout-and-drawing/before-finalization checkpoints cannot be exercised through the public contract without production-only fault injection, which the test-only boundary forbids. The limitation is recorded in the test class, PLANS.md, and the changelog.

Failure/pass-through: genuinely covered for the reachable reasons. Pass-through for IneligibleSeries/Season, MatchNotEligible (Ambiguous), NoMetadata, NoDisplayableValue, and SourceUnavailable all assert Status/reason and no artifact fields. Bounded failures assert exactly one reason, no artifact, and unchanged source bytes for SourceByteLimitExceeded, SourceDimensionLimitExceeded, OutputByteLimitExceeded (derived output), ContrastTooLow, ColorPolicyInvalid, FontUnavailable (bogus resource logical name, reached pre-native), and (guarded) UnsupportedInput and MalformedSource (descriptor/decoded-dimension mismatch).

Failure limitation (non-blocking): NativeAssetUnavailable, DecodeFailed, EncodeFailed, RenderError, and FontInvalid are not asserted as RenderResult reasons. The environment guard demonstrates that a missing native runtime makes the forced run fail (DllNotFoundException from the Skia fixture) rather than silently pass, but it does not assert the renderer's NativeAssetUnavailable mapping. These defensive mappings are not deterministically inducible through the public contract without fault injection or a corrupt bundled resource (only one embedded resource exists), so the declared limitation is acceptable for a test-only task and is recorded in the worker report and docs.

Build/test evidence reproduced independently on a clean tree: ./build.sh restore (locked, up-to-date), clean rm -rf bin/obj then ./build.sh restore/build -> 0 warnings 0 errors, ./build.sh test -> 554 passed / 0 failed / 21 skipped / 575 total, forced native full suite -> 575 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped, ./build.sh package -> succeeded and produced artifacts/ArrTags_0.1.0.0.zip. The RendererBehavior filter reports exactly 51 cases (40 unguarded, 11 guarded: 5 dimension + 4 format + 2 failure). Guard honesty re-confirmed: ARRTAGS_SKIA_COMPAT=1 without the pinned sysroot on LD_LIBRARY_PATH fails 4 RendererBehaviorFormatTests with DllNotFoundException; the skip occurs only when the flag is unset.

Task 4.11 boundary respected: no golden-image baselines, no fixed byte/hash oracle for the behavior matrix, no cross-runtime tolerance, and no ICC fail-closed behavior. Task 4.10 boundary respected: no renderer configuration model or new fingerprint. Documentation (PLANS.md status paragraph and checkbox, README, docs/changelog.md) accurately reflects the implementation and the reproduced counts.
